name: customer-use-cases-section
purpose: The "what teams use it for" band of a product page: a three-column frame whose first cell carries the band's overline, headline, lead and one call to action, followed by one cell per use case. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'customer-use-cases-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `card-grid`, `registration-frame`, `eyebrow`, `feature-item` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.
useWhen: Use CustomerUseCasesSection when the band's title sits in the first grid cell with one action.
On a product or solution page, right after the opening band, to name the concrete jobs the product is bought for. It is the one use-case band of a product page.
Whenever a page needs three to six short, icon-led use cases with one link out to the documentation.
avoidWhen: For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles-section`.
For use cases that each link to their own page, or any grid of claims with no single action → use `capability-grid-section`.
Inside another band's cell → compose `feature-item` directly.
related: `feature-item` — the icon, title and description cell each use case is rendered with.
`card-grid` — the frame grid this band lays its cells in.
bestPractices: On a product page give exactly four `items`; the first cell spans two rows at `lg`, so four cases fill the grid exactly. Elsewhere keep to four or so.
Write `title` as the heading the page's outline needs; it is the band's `h2`.
Give `primaryAction` an `href` to the documentation and set `trailing` so the chevron reads as "go".
Leave `eyebrow` as the product name; it is the overline the reader scans first.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Eyebrow above the headline in the title cell, closed by the blinking cursor.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2` in the title cell.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: Button pinned to the foot of the title cell; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent.

props.name: items
props.doc: The use cases rendered as frame cells, in order; each item is `{ icon, title, description }`.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it.
